newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline slips, Polish demand may resurface.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline slips, Polish demand may resurface.

text.p: NWE gasoline barges edged lower in quiet activity but a noted ARA buyer in the last week resurfaced for a small parcel, traders said.

Looking east, some traders said demand may soon resurface from Poland even though the Gdansk refinery said on Tuesday that all its gasoline requirements were met for its second quarter maintenance turnaround.

NWE cargo action was thin and appeared destined to wait for U.S. inventory data due out later on Tuesday. Stronger clues into gasoline demand across the Atlantic and Wednesday's expiry of the prompt NYMEX products also silenced cash deals.
Eurograde barges slipped $2 to $194/$196 and regular unleaded fell the same amount to $189/$191 fob ARA.
A Scandanavian trader was believed to have bought 2,000 tonnes of Rotterdam running refinery material for May at $196 fob, adding on to its recent purchases, traders said.
Premium unleaded cargoes were notionally unchanged at $201/$205 cif. Regular unleaded held at $194/$198 after a 9,000 tonne cargo was placed on Monday at $195.25 into Hamburg, traders said.
"The cargo market is extremely thin," a trader in Germany said. "On the one hand there is not much product around but there are not the prompt enquiries."

In Poland, a trader at the 60,000 barrel per day Gdansk refinery said it will not need to buy spot gasoline during its scheduled maintenance turnaround that started on Monday and will last until June 20.
Term contracts totalling 140,000 tonnes of Eurograde and regular unleaded have already covered its requirements, the trader said.
But another source said Poland's refineries, including Gdansk, may come back into the market in the second half of the second quarter to meet its needs for the summer.

"I expect more demand to come at the end of the second quarter from Poland," for Eurograde and low octane material, the source said. "We're pretty bullish for May and June...We've seen very little since the buying spree in April."
He said one of Poland's smaller refineries had bought two parcels of about 6,500 tonnes each recently.
